## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Paṭhamaaniyata* ("First Undetermined Rule", Bu-Vb Ay1) constitutes the opening rule of the *Aniyata* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule regulates cases where a trustworthy female lay disciple witnesses a monk sitting privately with a woman in a secluded, concealed location suitable for sexual intercourse. If she accuses the monk of an offense entailing expulsion (*pārājika*), formal suspension (*saṅghādisesa*), or confession (*pācittiya*), and the monk admits to having committed the act, he is adjudicated according to whichever of the three classes of offense he acknowledges [SuttaCentral]. The text includes the canonical framing narrative, the formulation of the training rule, and the word commentary (*padabhājaniya*), translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
This undetermined classification is shared across early Buddhist monastic codes. SuttaCentral records full parallels in the corresponding *Prātimokṣasūtra* and *Vinayavibhaṅga* texts of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya lineages preserved in Sanskrit, Classical Chinese, and Classical Tibetan, as well as the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and *Bhikkhu Parivāra* [SuttaCentral]. In addition, SuttaCentral notes internal passage-level parallels with *Aniyata* 2 and *Pācittiya* rules 30, 44, and 45 [SuttaCentral]. Machine text analysis via DharmaNexus confirms this heavy intra-Vinaya reuse, showing extensive shared material with *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Aniyata* 2 (most notably §2.2.43–3.9), the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha*, and *Pācittiya* rules 44, 45, 6, 7, and 30, alongside Vinaya commentaries such as the *Vinayavinicchaya-ṭīkā* and *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇīpurāṇa-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments by DharmaNexus also match sections of the text with Sanskrit *Prātimokṣasūtra* materials and Tibetan canonical translations, including the Mūlasarvāstivāda *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-2) and the *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
